bands.d: You are ahead of most fintech apps we see. Keep the annual VAPT and record-retention discipline current, and re-run this whenever you add a new payment flow or lending feature.

The foundations are there. Close the remaining controls in order — confirm your RBI category, then verify data localisation and audit logging — and get the licensing questions in front of a fintech compliance lawyer soon.

Several unchecked items here are infrastructure decisions, not paperwork — data localisation and audit logging in particular are expensive to retrofit. Get a compliance lawyer and a technical audit involved before you scale further.

A low score here is fixable, but not on a short timeline if you are already processing real transactions. First establish exactly which RBI category applies to you, then get a qualified fintech lawyer involved before building further.

items.t: We know exactly which RBI category we fall under
items.s: Payment aggregator, lending service provider, NBFC partner, or none of the above

items.t: Payments run through an already-licensed aggregator
items.s: Razorpay, Cashfree or similar — not a payment flow we built and hold ourselves

items.t: Every transaction has a genuine second authentication factor
items.s: AFA-compliant — not a single password or OTP alone where two factors are required

items.t: Payment and transaction data is stored on servers located in India
items.s: Data localisation — not a foreign-only cloud region for anything payment-related

items.t: If we lend money, we have NBFC registration or an LSP partnership
items.s: Not applicable if you don't originate or facilitate loans

items.t: KYC and AML checks run on every user per RBI's Master Direction
items.s: Automated, not a manual process someone can skip under pressure

items.t: We've had an annual VAPT covering the app, infrastructure and APIs
items.s: Addressing the OWASP Top 10 plus business logic flaws, with remediation verified

items.t: Transaction records, KYC documents and audit logs are retained for 5 years
items.s: With a system that actually enforces the retention, not a policy on paper

items.t: We could detect a fraud incident and report it to RBI within the required window
items.s: Logging and alerting good enough to know it happened and notify on time

items.t: Our DPDP Act consent and data-handling obligations are handled separately
items.s: RBI compliance does not replace India's data protection law — both apply

footnote: Nothing you tick is sent anywhere — this runs entirely in your browser.
